intelligence.enrichment: Sodium is a metal stored in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with oxygen and water and produces much heat. Phosphorus is stored in water because it catches fire when exposed to atmospheric air, while sulfur placed in water shows no reaction. The way a substance reacts with oxygen, air, or water determines the storage condition that prevents dangerous reaction. The learner correctly applies this rule: Sodium is a metal stored in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with oxygen and water and produces much heat. Phosphorus is stored in water because it catches fire when exposed to atmospheric air, while sulfur placed in water shows no reaction. All reactive substances need the same storage liquid; the liquid just keeps them covered.
